brief: BofA raises 2026 S&P 500 EPS to $365, up 33%, from $345, after 2Q EPS grew 50% year over year, or 32% excluding GOOGL and AMZN investment mark-ups, against 22% consensus, with above-consensus guides running 2.3 times below-consensus ones. It launches 2027 at $410, up 12%, below bottom-up consensus and above top-down. Economists' 2.2% real GDP growth would historically imply high-single-digit EPS growth. BofA argues the AI investment cycle, manufacturing recovery and productivity gains keep growth above trend instead. The risk is concentration: five stocks are a record 27% of next-twelve-month index earnings, Tech and the Mag 7 are 50%, and semis supply over 60% of 2027 consensus growth. Margin expansion slows from 2.6ppt to 0.6ppt as hyperscaler depreciation rises from 10% to 12% of revenue and capex depresses free cash flow relative to net income. Tariff refunds add 0-5% to 2026 GAAP EPS. Despite the fundamentals, BofA stays cautious on equities near term on liquidity, geopolitics, sticky inflation, seasonality, and the history that returns average 7.8% when EPS growth is above trend but decelerating. Its year-end target implies 3% downside.
